targets.title: Frame-header decode, canonical 7/16/64-bit payload lengths, masking
targets.statement: The shipped frame-header decoder and mask function: translateSingleFrame / translateSingleFramePayloadLength decode the 7-bit inline, 126->16-bit, and 127->64-bit big-endian payload-length forms with checked arithmetic (sign-carrying BigInteger parse, explicit >Integer.MAX_VALUE / >maxFrameSize / <0 rejection), and the XOR mask loop is applied on encode for the client role and removed on decode. Proof obligations bind to these shipped behaviors only.

java_authority.behavior: translateSingleFrame: FIN/RSV/opcode/mask-bit header decode; realpacketsize accumulation with translateSingleFrameCheckPacketSize (552-555); decode-side unmask XOR loop over the 4-byte key (558-563); checkAlloc-guarded payload allocation (557).

translateSingleFramePayloadLength: 7-bit inline lengths; 126 -> 16-bit and 127 -> 64-bit big-endian decode via sign-carrying BigInteger; control frames with >125 octets rejected at the escape (617-620); the shipped decoder does NOT reject non-minimal 16/64-bit encodings.
translateSingleFrameCheckLengthLimit: length > Integer.MAX_VALUE, length > maxFrameSize, and length < 0 all throw LimitExceededException — the shipped checked-arithmetic boundary.
createByteBufferFromFramedata: role masking (mask = role == Role.CLIENT at 480); 4-byte random mask key emission and XOR loop (511-517); 126/127 marker bytes and length-byte emission (497-510).
getSizeBytes: encode-side size-class selection (<=125 -> 1, <=65535 -> 2, else 8).
toByteArray: big-endian emission of the encoded payload length.

targets.statement: Every frame-path allocation is guarded by the shipped Draft.checkAlloc (negative byte counts throw InvalidDataException(PROTOCOL_ERROR)) and bounded by maxFrameSize via translateSingleFrameCheckLengthLimit. Proof obligations for allocation caps bind to these shipped guards.

translateSingleFrame: checkAlloc-guarded payload allocation (557) after packet-size revalidation (555).
translateFrame incomplete-frame path: checkAlloc-guarded buffer growth for extendedframe (749) and incompleteframe (768).

targets.title: Control-frame constraints (<=125 octets, opcode discrimination, dispatch)
targets.statement: Control frames (CLOSING/PING/PONG) with payload length above 125 octets are rejected at the 16/64-bit length escape; opcodes are discriminated by fromOpcode/toOpcode with unknown opcodes rejected; processFrame dispatches close/ping/pong in the shipped order. Proof obligations bind to these shipped constraints.

java_authority.behavior: translateSingleFramePayloadLength: PING/PONG/CLOSING reaching the >125 escape throw InvalidFrameException("more than 125 octets").
processFrame: CLOSING -> processFrameClosing, PING -> onWebsocketPing, PONG -> updateLastPong + onWebsocketPong, data frames -> continuation/fin handling.
fromOpcode/toOpcode: opcode discrimination; unknown opcode bytes throw InvalidFrameException.

targets.title: Server handshake accept predicate and Sec-WebSocket-Accept derivation
targets.statement: The SHIPPED server accept predicate is permissive: acceptHandshakeAsServer gates only readVersion(handshake) == 13 (any Integer.parseInt spelling after trim), and postProcessHandshakeResponseAsServer rejects only a null/empty Sec-WebSocket-Key before deriving Sec-WebSocket-Accept via the RFC 6455 SHA-1 derivation over the trimmed key. Draft.basicAccept's Upgrade/Connection validation runs only on the client path. Proof obligations for accept-derivation encode this shipped predicate; RFC-stricter reject language is valid only as a ledgered behavior delta.

java_authority.behavior: acceptHandshakeAsServer: NOT_MATCHED only when readVersion != 13; extension/protocol matching accepts with the shipped defaults (DefaultExtension and Protocol("")).
readVersion: Integer.parseInt after trim — '+13', '0013', ' 13 ' all read as 13; unparseable values read as -1.
postProcessHandshakeResponseAsServer: throws InvalidHandshakeException only for a missing/empty Sec-WebSocket-Key; sets Sec-WebSocket-Accept from generateFinalKey.
generateFinalKey: SHA-1 over trimmed key + RFC 6455 GUID, Base64-encoded — the accept derivation equals the RFC value.

targets.title: Terminal close is absorbing with exactly-once terminal delivery
targets.statement: closeConnection is the only terminal transition: it is monitor-guarded, delivers onWebsocketClose exactly once, resets the draft, and sets CLOSED; re-entry returns immediately. flushAndClose's latch makes close initiation idempotent and records the close code/message/remote triple delivered verbatim in the terminal event. Proof obligations bind to these shipped semantics.

java_authority.behavior: closeConnection: immediate return when already CLOSED (531-533); exactly-once onWebsocketClose (556-558); draft reset (561-563); readyState = CLOSED (566).
flushAndClose: flushandclosestate latch makes initiation idempotent; records closecode/closemessage/closedremotely; onWebsocketClosing delivered once.

targets.title: Connection state machine: no transition escapes CLOSED
targets.statement: The four shipped states NOT_YET_CONNECTED/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED transition only forward: open() sets OPEN from the handshake-complete path, close() initiates CLOSING under the monitor, eot() funnels every EOF into closeConnection, and no shipped path leaves CLOSED. The decode gate processes frames only in OPEN. Proof obligations bind to these shipped transitions.

java_authority.behavior: ReadyState: the closed four-state vocabulary NOT_YET_CONNECTED, OPEN, CLOSING, CLOSED.
close(int,String,boolean): monitor-guarded CLOSING transition with single close-frame send; no-ops once CLOSING/CLOSED.
open: readyState = OPEN exactly once from the completed-handshake path; onWebsocketOpen delivered.
eot: every EOF dispatch funnels into closeConnection (NEVER_CONNECTED / latched code / NORMAL / ABNORMAL_CLOSE); no path resurrects a closed connection.
decode: frames are decoded only in OPEN; NOT_YET_CONNECTED bytes go to decodeHandshake; no state regression from the decode path.

targets.title: Total UTF-8 validation of text payloads
targets.statement: Text payloads are validated by the shipped CharsetDecoder configured with CodingErrorAction.REPORT: every malformed or unmappable sequence throws InvalidDataException(NO_UTF8), and fragmented text is additionally checked incrementally by isValidUTF8. The Rust port must reject the identical sequence set. Proof obligations bind to these shipped validators.

java_authority.behavior: stringUtf8: CharsetDecoder with CodingErrorAction.REPORT (44); CharacterCodingException maps to InvalidDataException(CloseFrame.NO_UTF8).
isValidUTF8: incremental DFA validity check applied to text fragments.
processFrameText: every complete text payload passes Charsetfunctions.stringUtf8 before onWebsocketMessage.

targets.title: Bounded fragmentation reassembly
targets.statement: Continuation reassembly appends to the buffer list only under checkBufferLimit: when the reassembled total exceeds maxFrameSize the list is cleared and LimitExceededException is thrown, so fragmented messages cannot grow without bound. Sequencing violations (unstarted or uncompleted sequences) are protocol errors. Proof obligations bind to these shipped bounds.

java_authority.behavior: checkBufferLimit: reassembly total > maxFrameSize clears the buffer list and throws LimitExceededException(maxFrameSize).
processFrameContinuousAndNonFin: continuation sequencing; unstarted continuation is a PROTOCOL_ERROR; fragmented text checked incrementally for UTF-8 validity.
processFrameIsFin: append + checkBufferLimit before reassembled delivery; buffer list cleared after delivery.
processFrameIsNotFin: sequence start; append under the cap; uncompleted-previous-sequence is a PROTOCOL_ERROR.

targets.title: Adapters carry no protocol logic
targets.statement: WebSocketImpl.decode is the single protocol ingress: the shipped I/O helpers move bytes verbatim between sockets and the engine and never interpret WebSocket framing or handshakes. The Rust adapters (US-018) must preserve this byte-stream transparency; the proof target prohibits protocol logic outside ws_core. Proof obligations bind to this shipped separation.

java_authority.behavior: decode(ByteBuffer): the single protocol ingress the adapters feed; adapters never interpret WebSocket bytes.
SocketChannelIOHelper.read/readMore: pure byte transport from the channel into the engine buffer; no protocol interpretation.
SocketChannelIOHelper.batch: drains engine-produced buffers to the socket verbatim; the only protocol-adjacent effect (server-role close-on-drain) is delegated back to the engine via closeConnection.

targets.title: Single-owner serialization replaces the shared-mutable connection state
targets.statement: Java's connection state is shared-mutable — unbounded outQueue/inQueue, one volatile readyState read cross-thread without the monitor, the synchronizeWriteObject write lock, and the instance monitor across close/closeConnection/flushAndClose. The port's single-owner design serializes commands and inbound actions through one owner per connection; race-visible Java interleavings are not corpus-encodable and Java fidelity is defined over serialized observable event sequences. Proof obligations bind to the owner-serialization design, never to racy Java interleavings.

java_authority.behavior: The shared mutable state the port serializes: unbounded outQueue/inQueue (96-102) and the volatile readyState (127) read cross-thread without the monitor.
write(List) under synchronizeWriteObject: multi-frame enqueue of one message is atomic against other senders — wire order within a message is observable.
The instance monitor across close/closeConnection/flushAndClose is the de-facto connection lock producing exactly-once close initiation and terminal delivery.

java_authority_members: org.java_websocket.WebSocketImpl (shared-mutable state consolidated into the single owner)
